# Liberal Democrats 2005 Manifesto Summary

## Core Principles

The Liberal Democrats' manifesto is built on three principles: **Freedom, Fairness, and Trust**. They position themselves as the "real alternative" to Labour and Conservatives, emphasising transparent costings and environmental sustainability throughout all policies.

## Key Policy Areas

### Healthcare
The party proposes free personal care for elderly and disabled people, quicker diagnosis for serious conditions, free eye and dental checks, and scrapping government targets that interfere with clinical decisions. They would recruit 8,000 more doctors, 12,000 nurses, and ban smoking in enclosed public spaces.

### Education
Central pledges include abolishing tuition and top-up fees (costed at £1.2 billion annually), cutting infant class sizes to 20 pupils by recruiting 21,000 teachers using the £1.5 billion Child Trust Fund, and guaranteeing qualified teachers for core subjects.

### Taxation and Economy
The manifesto promises to replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax based on ability to pay, saving typical households £450 annually. A 50% tax rate on incomes exceeding £100,000 would fund education and elderly care reforms. The party commits to scrapping the DTI and opposing ID cards.

### Crime and Justice
Proposals include 10,000 additional police officers (funded by cancelling ID cards), community justice panels, tougher action on anti-social behaviour, and firm opposition to detention without trial.

### Pensions
The party proposes a "Citizen's Pension" based on residency rather than national insurance contributions, benefiting 2.8 million women. Pensioners over 75 would receive at least £109.45 weekly.

### International Affairs
The manifesto opposes the Iraq War while supporting EU membership and reform. It commits to reaching 0.7% of GNI for international aid and reforming trade policies favouring developing nations.

### Environment
Environmental policies include 20% renewable electricity by 2020, opposing nuclear replacement, promoting recycling, and introducing carbon taxes.
